paper.title_en: A phenomenological decomposition of SRC-inspired occupation effects in imbalanced Fermi superfluids
paper.abstract_en: Imbalanced two-component Fermi superfluids are usually formulated with sharp Fermi-step occupations, although interacting systems exhibit depletion below the Fermi surface and a high-momentum tail. We introduce a sector-resolved phenomenological framework in which one prescribed short-range-correlation (SRC)-inspired momentum distribution modifies either the anomalous pairing contribution (model P), the imbalance-induced blocking term (model B), or both (model P+B). The four realizations---ideal, P, B, and P+B---are compared through the grand-potential landscape and through a fixed-density reconstruction of the paired/phase-separated to polarized-normal boundary in three and two dimensions. In both dimensionalities, the pairing-sector modification accounts for nearly all of the reduction in the critical polarization, whereas the blocking-sector correction remains subdominant. Consequently, the phase boundaries form two nearly degenerate pairs, ideal $\simeq$ B and P $\simeq$ P+B. These results quantify, within the stated phenomenological construction, how a prescribed SRC-inspired occupation propagates separately through the pairing and blocking sectors of an imbalanced superfluid.
